title: Home Dashboard
description: The customizable Home screen widget grid — tire pressure, temperatures, fuel, battery, turbo, power, and octane learning, all sourced from your vehicle's CAN bus.
content:
## Home Dashboard

The **Home** tab is a customizable grid of live widget cards, each showing a different set of
vehicle data decoded from the CAN bus your **N-Link** is connected to. Add, remove, and reorder
widgets to build the dashboard that matters for your car.

Above the widget grid, supported vehicles show an interactive [3D model of your
car](/docs/app/dashboard/vehicle-viewer) instead of a static photo — see that page for rotating it
and changing its paint.

## Available widgets

Which widgets are available depends on your selected vehicle — for example, octane learning only
appears for vehicles that support it.

The default layout on first launch pairs **Tire Pressure** and **Fuel** on top, a full-width
**Car Health** card in the middle, then **Battery** and **Turbo** beneath, followed by **Power &
Torque** and **Octane**.

## Tap a card for details

Tapping any widget opens a full detail screen for that signal, including a short history chart
where available (for example, Car Health shows recent coolant, oil, and ambient temperature
trends, not just the current reading).

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Home dashboard grid with several widget cards, and one detail screen opened from a tap. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the Home dashboard and a widget detail screen. To be added.*

## Add, remove, and reorder widgets

## Related

* [Pairing & Connecting](/docs/app/pairing) — connect your N-Link before dashboard widgets show
  live data.
* [3D Vehicle Viewer](/docs/app/dashboard/vehicle-viewer) — the interactive car model above the
  widget grid.
* [Octane Learning](/docs/app/dashboard/octane-learning) — the full explainer behind the Octane
  Learning widget.
* [Data Lab: EK1 Pro vs. KDMLink](/docs/blog/ek1-pro-vs-kdmlink) — why KDMLink's direct CAN
  capture gives these widgets a much higher update rate than diagnostic-polling loggers.

title: Octane Learning
description: What octane/knock learning is, how KDMLink tracks it from your CAN bus, and how to confirm it's finished after a refuel.
content:
## Octane Learning

After every refuel, your ECU restarts its knock-adaptation cycle and temporarily caps peak boost
until it verifies the new fuel's quality. The **Octane Learning** screen shows where your car is
in that cycle. Open it from the **Octane Learning** widget on [Home](/docs/app/dashboard), or from
the Fuel Quality card on the Turbo widget's detail screen.

## Learning cycle

The status hero at the top shows one of four phases:

A checklist below the status shows the same cycle as steps (relearn triggered, adaptation
stage(s), learned), checking each one off as your car reports it.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Octane Learning screen — status hero and learning-cycle checklist. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the Octane Learning screen. To be added.*

## Why it isn't always instant

Your car doesn't broadcast the exact moment learning finishes. On vehicles that broadcast ECU
progress flags, KDMLink reads those directly, but the final "Learned" confirmation can still lag
a drive or two behind. On vehicles that don't broadcast progress at all, KDMLink tracks the cycle
from the refuel itself and only confirms completion from the boost behavior of a full-throttle
pull.

## Confirming with a pull

On vehicles without a broadcast status flag, the screen shows a **Verify with a Pull** section:
on a closed course, one full-throttle pull through the vehicle's verification RPM band (shown on
screen) in 3rd or 4th gear. KDMLink reads the boost behavior through that pull to confirm learned
vs. still-clamped instantly, and shows the last pull's verdict.

## Related

* [Home Dashboard](/docs/app/dashboard) — the Octane Learning widget that links here.

title: 3D Vehicle Viewer
description: The interactive 3D car on the Home tab — rotate it, hold to repaint it, and how the color you pick is saved.
content:
## 3D Vehicle Viewer

At the top of the **Home** tab, KDMLink renders your car as an interactive 3D model instead of a
static photo — for the vehicles it has a model for. Drag left or right to spin it around, or press
and hold it to change its paint.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Home tab with the 3D car rendered above the widget grid. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the 3D vehicle viewer on Home. To be added.*

## Rotating the car

The model is locked to a side-profile camera angle — it doesn't tilt up or down — but you can drag
horizontally to orbit it around and view any angle. Vertical drags pass through to the Home tab's
scroll instead of moving the car.

## Repainting your car

Press and hold the car for about a second to open the **Paint** sheet.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Paint sheet open over the 3D car — stock swatches and the color wheel. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the Paint sheet. To be added.*

## If the model doesn't load

If the 3D model fails to load — a slow connection to a bundled asset, an unsupported device, or a
timeout — KDMLink falls back to the same static vehicle image used for cars without a 3D model, so
Home always shows something in that spot.

## Related

* [Home Dashboard](/docs/app/dashboard) — the widget grid that sits below the vehicle viewer.
* [Sessions](/docs/app/sessions) — shared session cards render your car using this same paint
  color.

title: Overview
description: An overview of the KDMLink app and its main features.
content:
## The App

Once installed and connected, KDMLink gives you a single place to monitor live data, record
logs, and connect those sessions with RaceChrono. The app has four tabs — **Home**, **Live**,
**Sessions**, and **Settings** — this page is a high-level overview of each; deeper features get
their own page over time.

## Main features

## Home

The **Home** tab is a customizable dashboard of live widget cards — tire pressure, coolant/oil/
ambient temperature, fuel level, battery voltage, boost pressure, horsepower/torque, and octane
learning status — each sourced from your vehicle's CAN bus. Add, remove, and reorder widgets, and
tap any card for a detail view with recent history. See
[Home Dashboard](/docs/app/dashboard) for the full widget list and how to customize it.

## Live

The **Live** tab is a real-time race dashboard with portrait and full-screen landscape layouts:
gear, a segmented shift light bar, drive mode, and other live signals update continuously while
the N-Link is streaming data. See [Live Race Dashboard](/docs/app/live) for the full field-by-field
breakdown of both layouts.

## Sessions (data logging)

Start and stop recordings from the **Sessions** tab to log a drive for later review. Past
sessions show peak values and personal records, and can be shared as text or a card image. See
[Sessions](/docs/app/sessions) for how recording, personal records, and sharing work.

## RaceChrono integration

Enable RaceChrono in **Settings** to stream KDMLink's CAN-derived vehicle data into your
RaceChrono sessions for lap analysis. See [RaceChrono Integration](/docs/app/racechrono) for setup
steps.

title: Live Race Dashboard
description: The full-screen real-time race dashboard — gear, RPM, shift lights, pedals, G-force, and drive mode, in portrait and landscape.
content:
## Live Race Dashboard

The **Live** tab is a real-time dashboard built for driving, not just glancing at. It updates
continuously while your N-Link is streaming, and switches layout automatically between portrait
and landscape.

## Portrait: Command Deck

Turn the phone upright for a scrollable "command deck" layout:

* **Main card** — boost pressure and drive mode on the left, a large gear readout in the center,
  RPM and speed on the right.
* **Pedals** — horizontal throttle (THR) and brake (BRK) bars with live percentages.
* **Engine tiles** — coolant temp, oil temp, intake temp, and oil pressure in a 2×2 grid.
* **Tire pressure** — a plain FL / FR / RL / RR grid, in psi.
* **Footer** — fuel level and 12V battery voltage.

On tablets, the engine tile grid and tire pressure card sit side by side instead of stacking.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Live tab portrait "Command Deck" layout on phone. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the Live tab in portrait. To be added.*

## Landscape: full-screen dashboard

Rotate to landscape and the Live tab goes full-screen (status bar hidden) for an immersive
dashboard:

* **Top strip** — a segmented shift-light bar that fills up with RPM, a drive-mode badge, and a
  LIVE/OFFLINE status pill.
* **Center** — a large gear digit with a left/right steering-angle bar underneath.
* **Side columns** — swipeable card stacks. The left column has boost/coolant/oil-temp/oil-pressure
  tiles, a G-force card (lateral, longitudinal, and peak G with a live plot), and a second tile
  page with fuel, odometer, ambient temperature, and voltage. The right column has a speed/RPM
  card with throttle and brake bars, and a tire-pressure grid.
* **Bottom strip** — telltale lamps for turn signals, ABS, ESC, TPMS, oil pressure, coolant/oil
  temperature, battery, and fuel, each lighting up in its warning color when active.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Live tab landscape full-screen dashboard. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the Live tab in landscape. To be added.*

## Drive mode

The mode box/badge shows your vehicle's active drive mode: **Normal**, **Eco**, **Sport**, **N**
(shown with the N logo), or **Custom**.

## G-force

The G-force card plots your current lateral and longitudinal acceleration as a dot inside a
2-ring gauge (rings at 1G and 2G), alongside live LAT/LON readings and the peak combined G
recorded since you opened the tab.

## Related

* [Home Dashboard](/docs/app/dashboard) — the customizable widget grid on the Home tab.
* [Sessions](/docs/app/sessions) — record what you see on Live for later review.
* [Pairing & Connecting](/docs/app/pairing) — required before Live shows data.

title: Pairing & Connecting
description: How KDMLink pairs with your N-Link over Bluetooth on iOS and Android, and what happens during a connection.
content:
## Pairing & Connecting

This page explains how the KDMLink app finds and pairs with your **N-Link** over Bluetooth, what
each step of the connection means, and how the process differs between iPhone and Android. If
you've already paired once and just need to reconnect — or you're switching phones — see
[Re-pairing & Reconnecting](/docs/app/pairing/repairing).

## How KDMLink pairing works

KDMLink does **not** scan for devices inside the app. Instead it hands off to your phone's
operating system to run the pairing picker, so you choose your N-Link from a trusted system
screen:

* **iPhone (iOS 18 and later)** — uses Apple's **AccessorySetupKit** picker.
* **Android (8.0 and later)** — uses Android's **CompanionDeviceManager** picker.

In both cases the app filters the list down to N-Link hardware only (by its Bluetooth service ID
and the `N-Link` name), so you should only ever see your own device. Once you pick it, the OS
remembers the pairing and hands the app a private reference it uses to reconnect later — no
scanning required next time.

{/* VIDEO PLACEHOLDER: short screen recording of the full first-time pairing flow (open app → tap Pair → system picker → connected). Add once recorded. */}

*🎥 Video placeholder — full first-time pairing walkthrough. To be added.*

## Pair your N-Link step by step

## What happens during a connection

When you pick your N-Link, KDMLink runs through a short sequence behind the scenes. Knowing the
stages helps when something stalls:

| Stage | What's happening |
| --- | --- |
| **Choose your N-Link** | The system picker is open, waiting for you to select the device. |
| **Connecting** | The app opens the Bluetooth connection and negotiates the data packet size. |
| **Pairing** | Your phone and the N-Link exchange security keys (bonding) so the link is encrypted. |
| **Configuring** | The app reads the N-Link's firmware info and turns on the live data feed. |
| **Connected / Streaming** | Live vehicle data is flowing. |
| **Connected (no data)** | The link is up but no vehicle data is arriving — see the note below. |

### Pairing differs slightly by platform

The end result is the same — a secure, encrypted Bluetooth link — but the two operating systems
get there differently:

* **iPhone** — iOS completes a "Just Works" pairing automatically the first time the app reads
  secured data from the N-Link, and saves the keys to the iOS keychain. The Bluetooth link may
  briefly drop during this security handshake; iOS reconnects on its own, so a momentary blip
  during first pairing is normal.
* **Android** — Android creates the secure bond explicitly. You may see a one-time system
  Bluetooth pairing prompt; accept it. Once bonded, the app confirms the encrypted link and
  moves on.

## Troubleshooting first-time pairing

* **N-Link doesn't appear in the picker** — confirm the car is on and the N-Link has power, wait
  a few seconds for it to start advertising, then tap **Pair Device** again. Make sure you're
  close to the vehicle.
* **Bluetooth is off** — the app will prompt you; turn Bluetooth on and retry.
* **Permission denied** — if you declined the Bluetooth prompt, KDMLink can't connect. Enable
  Bluetooth permission for KDMLink in your phone's **Settings**, then try again.
* **iPhone says it needs iOS 18** — AccessorySetupKit pairing requires iOS 18 or later. Update
  iOS, then retry.
* **Pairing stalls or fails** — tap **Try again**. If it keeps failing, power the vehicle off and
  back on to restart the N-Link, then pair again.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: app pairing-failed / error state with the "Try again" button. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the pairing error state. To be added.*

## Next step

Already paired and just need to get back online, switch phones, or remove a device? See
[Re-pairing & Reconnecting](/docs/app/pairing/repairing).

title: Re-pairing & Reconnecting
description: How KDMLink reconnects to a paired N-Link, how to forget a device, and how to re-pair after switching phones or clearing the bond.
content:
## Re-pairing & Reconnecting

Once you've [paired your N-Link](/docs/app/pairing) the first time, KDMLink remembers it and
reconnects automatically — you normally never touch the pairing screen again. This page covers
what "reconnecting" looks like day to day, the difference between **reconnecting** and
**re-pairing**, how to **forget** a device, and how to recover when the connection won't come
back.

## Reconnecting vs. re-pairing

These two sound alike but mean different things:

* **Reconnecting** — re-establishing the Bluetooth link to a device you've **already paired**.
  This is automatic and needs no system picker. It happens every time you start the car or open
  the app.
* **Re-pairing** — pairing the N-Link again **from scratch** through the system picker. You only
  need this if the pairing was removed — for example you forgot the device, switched phones, or
  cleared the bond in your phone's Bluetooth settings.

## Automatic reconnect (the normal case)

Because the pairing is owned by your phone's operating system, KDMLink doesn't scan or show a
picker to reconnect. When the app opens or the N-Link powers up, it connects straight to the
remembered device by its saved reference.

* KDMLink keeps trying if the N-Link isn't in range yet, **backing off gradually** between
  attempts (about 5s, then 10s, 20s, 40s, up to 60s) so it doesn't drain your battery.
* If an active connection drops unexpectedly, the app attempts a quick reconnect within a couple
  of seconds.

{/* VIDEO PLACEHOLDER: screen recording showing the app auto-reconnecting on app open / car start. */}

*🎥 Video placeholder — app reconnecting automatically. To be added.*

## Manage paired devices in the app

The **Connections** screen lists your remembered N-Link devices and lets you connect, disconnect,
or forget them.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: app Connections screen showing the status card and paired-devices list. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the Connections screen with a paired N-Link. To be added.*

* **Connect** — tap **Connect** on a remembered device to reconnect manually.
* **Disconnect** — tap **Disconnect** to drop the link on purpose. While you stay disconnected
  this way, the app won't auto-reconnect until you reconnect or reopen the app.
* **Pair a new device** — opens the system picker to add another N-Link.
* **Forget** — swipe a device left and confirm to remove it (see below).

## Forget a device

Forgetting removes the N-Link from KDMLink **and** clears the pairing your phone's operating
system was holding. Use it when you're selling the N-Link, switching cars, or want a clean slate
before re-pairing.

After forgetting, the N-Link will **no longer auto-connect**. To use it again you'll need to
re-pair it from the system picker.

## Re-pair your N-Link

Re-pair when the previous pairing is gone or broken. Common reasons:

* You **forgot** the device (in the app or in your phone's Bluetooth settings).
* You **switched to a new phone** — pairings don't transfer.
* The N-Link was paired to **someone else's phone** and you're setting it up on yours.
* The connection is stuck and a full reset is the fastest fix.

The re-pair flow is the same as first-time pairing:

## Troubleshooting reconnection

* **Won't reconnect on its own** — make sure the car is on (the N-Link only has power with the
  ignition on) and your phone is nearby with Bluetooth enabled. Open the **Connections** screen
  and tap **Connect**.
* **Stuck on "Connecting…"** — power the vehicle off and back on to restart the N-Link, then try
  **Connect** again.
* **Connected but no data** — the link is up but no vehicle data is arriving. Confirm the car is
  running and the [N-Link install](/docs/installation/n-link) is fully seated. If it persists, a
  forget-and-re-pair usually clears it.
* **Keeps dropping mid-drive** — keep your phone within range and avoid blocking it with metal or
  thick cases. If drops continue, forget the device and re-pair.
* **Nothing works** — [forget the device](#forget-a-device) and [re-pair](#re-pair-your-n-link)
  from scratch. This is the most reliable reset and clears any stale pairing on the phone.

{/* VIDEO PLACEHOLDER: troubleshooting walkthrough — forget then re-pair to recover a stuck connection. */}

*🎥 Video placeholder — forget-and-re-pair recovery. To be added.*

## Related

* [Pairing & Connecting](/docs/app/pairing) — first-time setup and what each connection stage means.
* [N-Link Hardware](/docs/installation/n-link) — install and power.
* [App Install & Setup](/docs/installation/app) — download and first run.

timing.

This is configured from **Settings → RaceChrono**.

title: Sessions
description: Record drives, track personal records, review peaks and charts, and share sessions from the Sessions tab.
content:
## Sessions

The **Sessions** tab records a drive's telemetry for later review, and tracks your all-time
personal bests across every recorded session.

## Recording a session

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Sessions tab timer card, and the active recording screen with the live speed gauge. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — starting and recording a session. To be added.*

## Personal Records

Above your session history, KDMLink tracks lifetime bests across all recorded sessions:

Each record shows the date it was set. Records update automatically as new sessions come in —
there's nothing to reset or configure.

## Past Sessions

Every completed session appears as a card with its name, date, duration, top speed, and drive
mode. Tap a card to open the full session detail, or swipe it away to delete (with a confirmation
prompt first).

### Session detail

Opening a session shows its full peak stats — top speed, peak boost, peak RPM, max G, peak power,
and peak torque — plus time-series charts for turbo boost, RPM, speed, and oil temperature over
the course of the drive.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Session detail screen with peak stats and charts. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — session detail with charts. To be added.*

## Sharing a session

Sessions can be shared two ways from the session detail screen: as plain text summarizing the
drive, or as a shareable card image with the session's stats laid out for posting. Both use your
device's native share sheet.

## Related

* [Live Race Dashboard](/docs/app/live) — what a session records while you drive.
* [RaceChrono Integration](/docs/app/racechrono) — stream the same data into RaceChrono instead of
  (or alongside) recording a KDMLink session.

title: What's New Walkthrough
description: The full-screen walkthrough KDMLink shows after install or an update that ships features worth announcing.
content:
## What's New Walkthrough

KDMLink occasionally shows a short, full-screen walkthrough when you open the app — a handful of
swipeable pages, each with a short looping demo clip, introducing a feature from a recent update.

## When it appears

The walkthrough shows once, automatically, the first time you reach the main app after installing
KDMLink or after updating to a version with new walkthrough content — you don't need to do
anything to trigger it. Once you've seen a given walkthrough, KDMLink remembers that and won't
show it again unless a later update ships new content.

{/* IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: What's New walkthrough — a page mid-swipe with its demo clip, title, and body text. */}

*📷 Image placeholder — the What's New walkthrough. To be added.*

## Current topics

## Getting through it

* **Swipe** left/right, or tap **Next**, to move between pages. Progress dots at the bottom show
  where you are.
* **Skip** (top right) closes the walkthrough immediately from any page except the last.
* On the last page, **Skip** is replaced by **Done**, since that's how you'd normally finish it.
* On Android, the system back button also closes it.

## Related

* [3D Vehicle Viewer](/docs/app/dashboard/vehicle-viewer) — the paint-picker walkthrough page
  covers this feature.
* [Home Dashboard](/docs/app/dashboard) — the widget-rearranging walkthrough page covers this
  feature.

title: EK1 Pro vs. KDMLink: Why Data Rate Changes the Result
description: A measured comparison of multi-channel EK1 Pro diagnostic logging and KDMLink direct CAN capture for virtual dyno, acceleration, shift, and boost analysis.
content:
*Data Lab · June 20, 2026 · 8 minute read*

## The short version

In a simultaneous road test, an EK1 Pro multi-channel enhanced-PID log delivered about **3.14
samples per second for each channel**. KDMLink captured the car's broadcast CAN data at up to
**72 samples per second per signal**.

That makes KDMLink's RPM, accelerator, throttle, speed, and intake-temperature data roughly
**23 times denser** in this test. The difference matters whenever the analysis depends on how
quickly a value changes: virtual dyno curves, acceleration timing, DCT shifts, boost response,
and synchronized cross-channel plots.

## Two different ways to get data from the car

The rate difference starts with how each log was collected.

| | EK1 Pro multi-channel log | KDMLink direct CAN capture |
|---|---|---|
| Method | Request an enhanced PID and wait for the ECU response | Listen to frames the vehicle already broadcasts |
| Measured per-channel rate | About **3.14 Hz** | Up to **72.3 Hz** |
| Adding channels | Shares the request/response budget | Broadcast signals continue arriving independently |
| Timing | Channels are read at different points in the polling cycle | Every received frame is timestamped on the same clock |

Diagnostic logging is a conversation. The logger requests one value, waits for the ECU to
reply, and moves to the next value. With several channels selected, it cycles through them.
Each individual channel therefore updates less often.

KDMLink listens to the powertrain CAN bus instead. RPM, pedal position, throttle, vehicle speed,
and other values are already being broadcast for the vehicle's control modules. KDMLink does
not need to request those values one at a time; it captures each frame as it arrives.

## What we measured

Both logs came from the same drive and were recorded simultaneously. The KDMLink capture ran
for about 55 seconds and contained 127,835 CAN frames. The EK1 Pro reference log contained 191
samples per selected channel over roughly 61 seconds.

| Signal | CAN ID | KDMLink | EK1 Pro | Measured advantage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Engine RPM | `0x080` | **72.3 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **23×** |
| Accelerator pedal | `0x080` | **72.3 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **23×** |
| Throttle position | `0x329` | **72.0 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **23×** |
| Vehicle speed | `0x316` | **71.9 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **23×** |
| Intake air temperature | `0x081` | **71.7 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **23×** |
| Wheel speed | `0x386` | **35.9 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **11×** |
| Boost pressure | `0x492` | **14.5 Hz** | 3.14 Hz | **4.6×** |

The exact KDMLink rate depends on how often the vehicle broadcasts each CAN ID. The important
part is that capturing one broadcast signal does not require KDMLink to pause the others.

## One pull, two very different traces

![Engine RPM captured by KDMLink at 72 Hz and sampled at the EK1 Pro cadence of 3 Hz](/data-logging/ek1-pro-vs-kdmlink-rpm.svg)

This 5.8-second window contains **468 KDMLink RPM points** and **16 points at the EK1 Pro
cadence**. Both traces describe the same pull, but they do not preserve the same information.
The dense trace resolves the launch, the RPM climb, and the sharp drop during the shift. The
sparse trace connects widely separated samples and rounds over fast transitions.

## A DCT shift can happen between two samples

![A DCT upshift resolved by KDMLink but missed at the EK1 Pro logging cadence](/data-logging/ek1-pro-vs-kdmlink-shift.svg)

During this shift, engine speed dropped by about 970 RPM in roughly 150 milliseconds. KDMLink
captured approximately 18 frames during the event. At 3.14 Hz, samples arrive about 318
milliseconds apart, so the entire torque interruption can fit between two RPM readings.

That resolution is useful for:

* Finding the exact start and end of a shift
* Separating a clean single-gear pull for dyno analysis
* Inspecting clutch slip or RPM flare
* Comparing torque intervention between shifts

## Why virtual dyno needs a high-rate RPM trace

A virtual dyno estimates power from the rate at which the engine accelerates. In simplified
form:

```text
power ∝ ω × (dω/dt)

where ω = engine speed in radians per second = 2π × RPM / 60
```

The critical term is `dω/dt`, the change in engine speed over time. Differentiation amplifies
noise, so a useful calculation needs enough samples to filter noise without erasing the shape
of the pull.

A four-second pull at 3 Hz provides only about 12 RPM points. At 72 Hz, the same pull provides
nearly 290. That additional data creates room to smooth noise while retaining torque peaks,
power roll-off, and shift boundaries.

![Virtual dyno curve calculated from the dense KDMLink trace and the sparse EK1 Pro cadence](/data-logging/ek1-pro-vs-kdmlink-dyno.svg)

For this pull, the 72 Hz calculation produces a continuous curve with a clear peak around
4,050–4,250 RPM. The 3 Hz version misses much of that peak and produces an artificial spike
near the top of the run. Those are sampling artifacts, not changes in the engine.

## Boost benefits too

![Boost response captured by KDMLink at 14.5 Hz and sampled at the EK1 Pro cadence of 3 Hz](/data-logging/ek1-pro-vs-kdmlink-boost.svg)

Boost is broadcast less often than RPM on this vehicle, but KDMLink still captured it at about
14.5 Hz—roughly 4.6 times the tested EK1 Pro per-channel rate. The denser trace preserves the
spool ramp and a brief pressure dip during the shift that the slower cadence smooths over.

For diagnosing an overboost event, wastegate response, or a shift-related pressure drop, the
short event between samples may be the event you needed to see.

## Synchronization matters as much as speed

In a request-and-response log, channels are polled one after another. The RPM, throttle, and
boost values shown on the same row may have been measured at different moments in the polling
cycle. During a launch or shift, a few hundred milliseconds of offset can change the meaning
of a cross-channel comparison.

KDMLink timestamps each received broadcast frame against one clock. The CAN IDs do not all
broadcast at the same frequency, but their timestamps share the same time base. That produces
more honest RPM-versus-throttle, boost-versus-RPM, and speed-versus-time analysis.

## Where EK1 Pro diagnostic polling still matters

Direct CAN capture is not a replacement for every diagnostic PID. Some values are not
broadcast on this vehicle's bus and must be requested from the ECU. Examples include AFR,
ignition timing, knock, and fuel-rail pressure.

An EK1 Pro can also return a single requested PID faster when fewer channels are selected. The
tradeoff is channel coverage: spending more of the request budget on one PID leaves less time
for the rest.

The practical distinction is:

* Use diagnostic requests for values the car does not broadcast.
* Use KDMLink's direct CAN capture when timing resolution and synchronization are central to
  the result.

## The takeaway

EK1 Pro and KDMLink are not simply two interfaces reading the same data in the same way. In the
tested setup, the EK1 Pro log requested multiple enhanced PIDs in sequence, while KDMLink
captured the vehicle's existing CAN broadcasts in parallel.

For steady-state checks, a few readings per second may be enough. For a virtual dyno, an
acceleration timer, a DCT shift, or boost-spool analysis, it is not. KDMLink's direct capture
preserves the fast changes that make those measurements useful.

## Test methodology

* Both files came from the same drive and were recorded simultaneously.
* The clocks were aligned by cross-correlating accelerator pedal and throttle. Correlation was
  0.994 for pedal and 0.997 for throttle after applying a 400 ms offset.
* The EK1 Pro cadence came from its actual sample timestamps: 191 samples per channel over
  approximately 61 seconds.
* KDMLink rates are frame counts divided by the 55-second capture duration.
* The cadence comparison sampled the broadcast RPM at the EK1 Pro timestamps, isolating the
  effect of sampling rate from differences in signal decoding.

## Compatible Vehicles

KDMLink is built for supported Hyundai N vehicles. Check this list before installing the
**N-Link** hardware or pairing the app.

## Supported N cars

| Vehicle | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Hyundai Veloster N | Plug and play. |
| Hyundai Elantra N | Wire tap method. |
| Hyundai Kona N | Plug and play. |
| Hyundai i20 N | Coming soon. |
| Hyundai i30 N | Coming soon. |
| Hyundai i30 Fastback N | Coming soon. |
| Hyundai IONIQ 5 N | Coming soon. |
| Hyundai IONIQ 6 N | Coming soon. |

N Line trims are not the same as full N vehicles. If your car is an N Line model, confirm
support before installing.

## Requirements

* KDMLink **N-Link** interface
* KDMLink app on iPhone or Android
* Supported Hyundai N vehicle
* Correct N-Link install method for your vehicle

## Install methods

* [**Plug and play**](/docs/installation/n-link/plug-and-play) — for supported vehicles where
  the N-Link can connect directly at the OBD-II port.
* [**Wire tap**](/docs/installation/n-link/wire-tap) — for supported vehicles that require
  tapping the correct signal and power wires for a clean N-Link connection.

## Next step

After confirming your vehicle is supported, continue to
[N-Link Hardware](/docs/installation/n-link) for install options.

title: Installation
description: Set up your N-Link hardware and install the KDMLink app.
content:
## Installation

Getting set up with KDMLink has two parts: installing the **N-Link** hardware in your vehicle,
and installing the **KDMLink app** on your phone.

## Download the app

* **iOS** — [Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/kdmlink/id6758346077)
* **Android** — Post your email to @KDMLink on Instagram for early access

## What you'll need

* A supported KDM vehicle
* A KDMLink **N-Link** interface device

Once you've installed the hardware and the app, head to [App Install & Setup](/docs/installation/app)
to pair your phone with the N-Link and verify the connection.

title: N-Link Hardware
description: How to install the KDMLink N-Link interface in your vehicle.
content:
## N-Link Hardware Install

The **N-Link** is the hardware interface that connects KDMLink to your vehicle for logging.
Choose the install method that matches your vehicle:

Check [Compatible Vehicles](/docs/compatible-vehicles) before choosing an install method. Once
the N-Link is installed and powered, head over to [App Install & Setup](/docs/installation/app)
to pair it with your phone.

## What's in the box

* N-Link module
* CAN bus harness (for plug-and-play installs) or wire-tap harness (for wire-tap installs)
* Power harness with inline fuse
* KDMLink sticker

## Before you start

Park the vehicle safely, turn it off, and confirm that your phone and vehicle are compatible.
For wire-tap installs, verify the exact wire locations for your vehicle before making any
connections. Required tools:

* Phillips screwdriver
* Pliers or fuse puller (for power harness fuse)
* Zip ties or double-sided tape to secure the N-Link and harnesses

## Compatibility

For vehicle, phone, and install-method requirements, see
[Compatible Vehicles](/docs/compatible-vehicles).

## Troubleshooting

* **No power** — confirm the connector or wire-tap power connection is fully seated.
* **N-Link does not appear in the app** — confirm the N-Link is powered, then continue to
  [App Install & Setup](/docs/installation/app).
* **Vehicle data not appearing in the app** — confirm the N-Link is properly connected to the
  vehicle's CAN bus (harness fully seated for plug-and-play, wire-tap connections secure and
  correctly matched), then reconnect in the app.

## Next step

Once the N-Link is installed and powered, continue to
[App Install & Setup](/docs/installation/app) to pair it with the KDMLink app.

title: Introduction
description: What KDMLink is and what you can do with it.
content:
## What is KDMLink?

**KDMLink** is a mobile data logging and RaceChrono integration app for Korean cars
(Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis). It pairs with the **N-Link** interface to read live data
from your vehicle, record sessions, and send the data where you need it from your phone.

## Who it's for

KDMLink is built for owners and track drivers of Korean performance cars who want clean,
phone-based logging and RaceChrono workflows.

## What you'll need

* A supported KDM vehicle
* A KDMLink **N-Link** interface device
* The KDMLink app installed on your iPhone (Android coming soon)

Check [Compatible Vehicles](/docs/compatible-vehicles), then head to
[Installation](/docs/installation) to set everything up.
